I’ve read the changed code paths. Now I’m checking for places outside the diff that still assume the v1 metadata branch exists, because that’s the most likely regression when `checkpoints_v2_only` stops dual-writing.

I found several existing code paths that switch behavior based on `IsCheckpointsV2Enabled()`. I’m sampling the main read paths now to make sure `checkpoints_v2_only` doesn’t accidentally route into v1 anywhere important, especially resume/rewind.

I have one likely behavior gap to verify, but before writing it up I’m running the targeted unit and integration tests that were added around this flag. That will tell me whether the new paths are at least covered and whether any nearby regressions already surface.

The focused unit tests passed immediately. The integration run is still in progress, so I’m waiting on that before I finalize the review and decide whether the gap is a real regression or just a missing edge-case test.

// TestV2Resume_SwitchBranchWithSession verifies that resume works when
// checkpoints_v2 is enabled. The session transcript should be read from
// v2 refs (/main for metadata, /full/* for raw transcript).
func TestV2Resume_SwitchBranchWithSession(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	env := NewTestEnv(t)
	defer env.Cleanup()

	// Setup repo with feature branch
	env.InitRepo()
	env.WriteFile("README.md", "# Test")
	env.WriteFile(".gitignore", ".entire/\n")
	env.GitAdd("README.md")
	env.GitAdd(".gitignore")
	env.GitCommit("Initial commit")
	env.GitCheckoutNewBranch("feature/v2-resume-test")

	// Initialize with checkpoints_v2 enabled
	env.InitEntireWithOptions(map[string]any{
		"checkpoints_v2": true,
	})

	// Create a session
	session := env.NewSession()
	err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmitWithPrompt(session.ID, "Create hello script")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	content := "puts 'Hello from v2 session'"
	env.WriteFile("hello.rb", content)

	session.CreateTranscript(
		"Create hello script",
		[]FileChange{{Path: "hello.rb", Content: content}},
	)
	err = env.SimulateStop(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Commit (triggers dual-write to v1 + v2)
	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Create hello script", "hello.rb")

	featureBranch := env.GetCurrentBranch()

	// Switch to master
	env.GitCheckoutBranch("master")
	assert.Equal(t, "master", env.GetCurrentBranch())

	// Run resume to switch back to feature branch
	output, err := env.RunResume(featureBranch)
	require.NoError(t, err, "resume failed: %s", output)

	// Verify we switched back
	assert.Equal(t, featureBranch, env.GetCurrentBranch())

	// Verify output contains session info and resume command
	assert.Contains(t, output, "Restored session", "output should contain 'Restored session'")
	assert.Contains(t, output, "claude -r", "output should contain resume command")

	// Verify transcript was restored
	transcriptFiles, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(env.ClaudeProjectDir, "*.jsonl"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.NotEmpty(t, transcriptFiles, "transcript should be restored to Claude project dir")
}

content.text: I found a more concrete regression candidate: `checkpoints_v2_only` takes effect from merged local settings, but the migration/discoverability messaging only keys off committed project settings. I’m pulling exact line numbers now because that means a local-only experiment can silently stop writing/pushing v1 before the repo has actually declared the migration.

- Medium: `checkpoints_v2_only` takes effect from merged local settings immediately, so a user can flip it on in `.entire/settings.local.json` and this branch will stop writing/pushing `entire/checkpoints/v1` in condensation and pre-push ([settings.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:427), [settings.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:446), [manual_commit_condensation.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:256), [manual_commit_push.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:31)). But the new migration/discoverability hint only looks at committed `HEAD:.entire/settings.json` ([push_common.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_common.go:145)), which means a local-only experiment can silently strand new checkpoints in v2 before the repo has actually declared the migration. I’d either make `checkpoints_v2_only` honor committed settings only, or emit a hard warning/block when it is enabled only via local overrides.

Targeted tests passed:
`go test ./cmd/entire/cli/settings ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy -run 'Test(IsCheckpointsV2|PrintSettingsCommitHint|IsCheckpointsV2OnlyCommitted|PrintCheckpointsV2OnlyMigrationHint)'`
and
`go test -tags integration ./cmd/entire/cli/integration_test -run 'TestV2(Only_FullWorkflow|Push_V2OnlySkipsV1Branch|Push_FullCycle|DualWrite_FullWorkflow)'`.

The gap above is not covered by the added tests.
Fix the review comments

I’m fixing the review feedback on `checkpoints_v2_only`. First I’m locating the existing settings/strategy paths and tests so I can make the behavior consistent without disturbing the rest of the v2 rollout.

I’ve confirmed the problem surface: the context-level helper reads merged local settings, while the migration hint reads committed project settings. I’m narrowing every `IsCheckpointsV2OnlyEnabled(ctx)` use now so I can switch only the strategy-affecting behavior to the committed view and keep the simple settings struct methods intact.

I’ve got the fix shape: make the runtime `checkpoints_v2_only` gate project-scoped instead of merged-local, then add tests that prove `.entire/settings.local.json` can’t silently turn off v1 writes/pushes. I’m reading the nearby helper and docs blocks before editing so the behavior and comments line up.
